userStories.title: Add mutation-check execution config and selector
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Add the opt-in `execution.mutationCheck` config subtree and expose it through a dedicated selector.

**Motivation** — RED proves tests exist, this proves they can fail meaningfully.

**Approach** — Add `MutationCheckConfigSchema` (`enabled` default `false`, `maxMutants` default `3`, `timeoutSeconds`), mount on `ExecutionConfigSchema`, add the per-package merge spread, and a `reshapeSelector`-based `mutation-check` config selector.

**Scope** — In: `src/config/schemas-execution.ts`, `src/config/merge.ts`, `src/config/selectors.ts`. Out: mutation generation, file mutation/revert logic, the deterministic operation, and story-orchestrator phase wiring.

**Interface**
```typescript
const mutationCheckConfigSelector = reshapeSelector("mutation-check", (c) => c.execution?.mutationCheck);
type MutationCheckConfig = ReturnType<typeof mutationCheckConfigSelector.select>;
```
acceptanceCriteria: Given the execution config with `mutationCheck` unset, when the config is parsed, then `config.execution.mutationCheck.enabled === false`.
Given the execution config with `mutationCheck` unset, when the config is parsed, then `config.execution.mutationCheck.maxMutants === 3`.
Given the execution config with `mutationCheck` unset, when the config is parsed, then `config.execution.mutationCheck.timeoutSeconds` is a positive integer.
Given a config where `mutationCheck.maxMutants` is set to `5`, when the config is parsed, then resolved `maxMutants === 5`.

Given a root config whose `mutationCheck.enabled` is `false` and a per-package override `{ execution: { mutationCheck: { enabled: true } } }`, when `mergePackageConfig()` merges them, then resolved `enabled === true` and `maxMutants` retains the root or default value.
Given a parsed config, when the `mutation-check` config selector is applied, then it returns an object exposing `enabled`, `maxMutants`, and `timeoutSeconds`.

routing.reasoning: This story adds one nested execution schema, one merge branch, and one selector in config modules that already have stable unit-test patterns.

userStories.title: Build deterministic mutation generation core
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Create the pure mutation-generation module for deterministic, language-aware spot checks.

**Motivation** — Mutation spot-checks close this hole by injecting deterministic bugs into the just-implemented code and confirming the story's own tests notice.

**Approach** — Create `src/verification/mutation/` with the shared types, the per-language operator tables (TS populated; python/go stubbed empty), and `generateMutants`. Pure and deterministic — no I/O.

**Scope** — In: `src/verification/mutation/{index,types,operators,mutator}.ts`. Out: file mutation/revert I/O, result classification, operation wiring, config, and phase integration.

**Interface** — Verbatim type surface from the spec: `Mutant`, `MutantOutcome`, `MutationOperator`, `SurvivingMutant`, and `generateMutants` exported from `src/verification/mutation`.
acceptanceCriteria: Given a source containing `a > b` and language `"typescript"`, when `generateMutants` is called, then it returns at least one `Mutant` whose `after` contains `a < b` and whose `operatorId` names a comparison-flip operator.
Given a source containing the boolean literal `true` and language `"typescript"`, when `generateMutants` is called, then it returns a `Mutant` whose `after` replaces that token with `false`.
Given a source containing `x + y` and language `"typescript"`, when `generateMutants` is called, then it returns a `Mutant` whose `after` contains `x - y`.
Given `generateMutants` returns a `Mutant`, when that `Mutant` is inspected, then it exposes `file`, `line` (1-indexed), `before`, `after`, and `operatorId`.
Given language `"python"`, when `generateMutants` is called, then it returns an empty array.
Given language `"go"`, when `generateMutants` is called, then it returns an empty array.
Given an `undefined` language, when `generateMutants` is called, then it returns an empty array.
Given a source with 10 operator-matchable lines and `max = 3`, when `generateMutants` is called, then it returns at most 3 `Mutant`s.
Given a source containing no operator-matchable tokens, when `generateMutants` is called, then it returns an empty array.

routing.reasoning: This story creates a new pure module with deterministic transformation rules and no runtime orchestration dependencies.

userStories.title: Add mutation apply, revert, and classification helpers
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Add the file-editing and outcome-classification layer for generated mutants.

**Motivation** — The gate is advisory: a false alarm costs one log line, never a blocked story.

**Approach** — Add `applyMutant`/`revertMutant` (file mutate/restore — **must use Bun-native `Bun.file()`/`Bun.write()`**, never Node `fs`) and `classifyMutant`. Extend the `src/verification/mutation` barrel with these exports.

**Scope** — In: `src/verification/mutation/{apply,classify}.ts`, `src/verification/mutation/index.ts`, and interpretation of `VerificationResult.status`. Out: config, mutation generation rules, deterministic operation wiring, and phase integration.

**Interface** — Verbatim callable surface from the spec: `applyMutant`, `revertMutant`, and `classifyMutant(result): MutantOutcome`.
acceptanceCriteria: Given a temp file the test creates, when `applyMutant(m)` is called, then reading the file back returns `m.after` on line `m.line`.
Given a temp file and a mutant `m`, when `applyMutant(m)` is followed by `revertMutant(m)`, then the file contents are byte-for-byte identical to the original contents.
Given a `VerificationResult` with `status: "TEST_FAILURE"`, when `classifyMutant` is called, then it returns `"killed"`.
Given a `VerificationResult` with `status: "SUCCESS"`, when `classifyMutant` is called, then it returns `"survived"`.
Given a `VerificationResult` whose `status` is `"ENVIRONMENTAL_FAILURE"`, `"ASSET_CHECK_FAILED"`, or `"TIMEOUT"`, when `classifyMutant` is called, then it returns `"errored"`.

routing.reasoning: This story adds a small Bun-native file mutation layer plus a direct status-to-outcome mapper on top of the new mutation types.

userStories.title: Implement the mutation-check deterministic operation
acceptanceCriteria: Given `mutationCheckOp` imported from the `@/operations` barrel, when it is inspected, then `kind === "deterministic"`, `name === "mutation-check"`, and `stage === "verify"`.

Given `mutationCheck.enabled === false`, when `mutationCheckOp.execute()` runs, then it returns `success: true` with an empty `survivors` list and never calls the injected `selectScopedTests` or `regression` deps.

Given injected `getChangedNonTestFiles` resolves to one TypeScript source file, its content yields one mutant, and injected `regression` returns `status: "SUCCESS"`, when `mutationCheckOp.execute()` runs, then it returns `success: true` and `survivors` contains one entry whose `file`, `line`, and `operatorId` identify that mutant.

Given the same setup as the previous criterion except injected `regression` returns `status: "TEST_FAILURE"`, when `mutationCheckOp.execute()` runs, then it returns `success: true` with an empty `survivors` list.

Given the same setup as the survivor criterion except injected `regression` returns `status: "TIMEOUT"`, when `mutationCheckOp.execute()` runs, then it returns `success: true` with an empty `survivors` list.
Given injected `detectLanguage` resolves to `"python"`, when `mutationCheckOp.execute()` runs, then it returns `success: true` with an empty `survivors` list and never calls injected `regression`.
Given `maxMutants === 2` and a changed file whose content yields 5 candidate mutants, when `mutationCheckOp.execute()` runs, then it calls injected `regression` at most 2 times.

Given a run where at least one mutant is executed, when `mutationCheckOp.execute()` calls injected `selectScopedTests`, then the input references the mutated file and the story's `storyGitRef`; and when it calls injected `regression`, then it uses the `effectiveCommand` returned by `selectScopedTests`.
Given an injected `regression` call throws, when `mutationCheckOp.execute()` runs, then it restores the mutated file to its original contents and returns `success: true`.

routing.reasoning: This story adds one new deterministic operation and barrel export by composing existing helpers with the same DI and regression patterns already used by verify-scoped.

userStories.title: Wire mutation-check into story-orchestrator phases and plan building
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Register the advisory mutation-check phase in the story-orchestrator and plan builder immediately after GREEN.

**Motivation** — Because the phase loop short-circuits on the first failing phase, GREEN is guaranteed before it runs. Because the phase is advisory (always `success: true`) and **not** listed in `STRICT_VERDICT_PHASE_NAMES`, it never short-circuits the downstream `verifier`/review phases.

**Approach** — Register `PhaseKind "mutation-check"` in `CANONICAL_ORDER` after `full-suite-gate`, add its `PHASE_KIND_TO_STATE_KEY`/`InternalBuildState` entries, keep it out of `STRICT_VERDICT_PHASE_NAMES`, add the `addMutationCheck` builder method, and wire `PlanInputs` + `build-plan-for-strategy`.

**Scope** — In: `src/execution/story-orchestrator/types.ts`, `src/execution/story-orchestrator/builder.ts`, `src/execution/plan-inputs.ts`, and `src/execution/build-plan-for-strategy.ts`. Out: mutation generation rules, mutation file I/O, and the mutation-check operation internals.

**Interface** — Verbatim seam from the spec: `PlanInputs` is extended with `mutationCheck?: MutationCheckInput` and `build-plan-for-strategy` conditionally calls `builder.addMutationCheck(...)` so the phase appears immediately after `full-suite-gate` when present.
acceptanceCriteria: Given `CANONICAL_ORDER`, when it is inspected, then it contains `"mutation-check"` at the index immediately following `"full-suite-gate"`.

Given `PHASE_KIND_TO_STATE_KEY` and `InternalBuildState`, when the mutation-check phase is registered, then `PHASE_KIND_TO_STATE_KEY["mutation-check"]` equals `"mutationCheck"` and `InternalBuildState` accepts a `mutationCheck` phase entry.
Given `STRICT_VERDICT_PHASE_NAMES`, when it is inspected, then `STRICT_VERDICT_PHASE_NAMES.has("mutation-check")` is `false`.

Given a plan built through the orchestrator builder with `addMutationCheck(input)`, `full-suite-gate` passing, and `mutationCheck.enabled` true, when the plan runs, then a spied `mutationCheckOp` is invoked after the `full-suite-gate` phase.

Given `PlanInputs` that include a `mutationCheck` input, when `buildPlanForStrategy()` builds the plan, then the ordered phases include a `"mutation-check"` phase; and given `PlanInputs` without that input, when `buildPlanForStrategy()` builds the plan, then it contains no `"mutation-check"` phase.
Given a `mutationCheckOp` result carrying a survivor with `success: true`, when the phase loop continues, then the subsequent `verifier` phase still executes.

routing.reasoning: This story extends existing phase-order and plan-builder tables in four files using an established add-phase pattern and explicit backward-compatibility checks.

analysis:
This feature extends an existing TypeScript/Bun verification pipeline rather than adding a new subsystem. The codebase already has the exact seams the spec cites: `greenfieldGateOp` is a deterministic operation in `src/operations/greenfield-gate.ts:47`, `verifyScopedOp` is a deterministic operation with DI and regression execution in `src/operations/verify-scoped.ts:59`, `getChangedNonTestFiles()` is in `src/verification/smart-runner.ts:399`, `selectScopedTests()` is in `src/test-runners/scoped-selection.ts:94`, `regression()` is in `src/verification/runners.ts:155`, and phase ordering is owned by `src/execution/story-orchestrator/types.ts`. That means the feature should follow existing deterministic-op and builder conventions rather than inventing a new orchestration mechanism.

The execution config is additive and has a direct precedent. `ExecutionConfigSchema` in `src/config/schemas-execution.ts:120` already mounts nested execution config blocks such as `regressionGate`, `smartTestRunner`, `worktreeDependencies`, and `flakeDetection`. `FlakeDetectionConfigSchema` at `src/config/schemas-execution.ts:110` is the closest template for a new nested execution subtree with defaults. Package-override merging is handled centrally in `src/config/merge.ts:71`; that file already deep-merges `execution.regressionGate` and `execution.flakeDetection`, so `execution.mutationCheck` must get the same field-wise merge treatment or package overrides will clobber root defaults. Selector design should follow `reshapeSelector()` in `src/config/selector.ts:62` and the selector registry in `src/config/selectors.ts:13`; the spec is correct that `pickSelector("mutation-check", "execution")` would return the wrong shape for the new op.

The mutation core is genuinely new code, but it fits the repo’s current verification layout. The repo already organizes verification utilities under `src/verification/`, with public exports managed by `src/verification/index.ts`. The spec’s proposed `src/verification/mutation/` subtree is therefore a good fit. The cleanest design boundary is the one the spec already defines: keep mutation generation pure and deterministic in `mutator.ts` and `operators.ts`, keep file-editing in `apply.ts`, and keep result-status interpretation in `classify.ts`. That separation aligns with the acceptance criteria split and avoids coupling the core mutation logic to git, test selection, or subprocess execution.

The main technical constraint is that `mutationCheckOp` combines two patterns that currently exist separately but not together. `greenfieldGateOp` shows the expected `DeterministicOperation` shape and config selection style, while `verifyScopedOp` shows the DI pattern, package config lookup, logger usage, and the `selectScopedTests()` -> `regression()` flow. `verifyScopedOp` also demonstrates that the operation should use `getLogger()` rather than expect a logger on `CallContext`, and that injected deps are the right way to make unit and integration tests run without real git or real test commands. `regression()` itself is only a thin wrapper over `runVerificationCore()` with a built-in sleep in `src/verification/runners.ts:155`, so the mutation spot-check budget is concretely bounded by `maxMutants` extra regression calls per story.

Phase integration is localized and should remain advisory. `PhaseKind`, `CANONICAL_ORDER`, `PHASE_KIND_TO_STATE_KEY`, `InternalBuildState`, and `STRICT_VERDICT_PHASE_NAMES` are defined in `src/execution/story-orchestrator/types.ts:65-228`. The current canonical order places `full-suite-gate` before `verifier` and `verify-scoped`, which is exactly the seam the spec wants. Because the phase loop short-circuits on failures, placing `mutation-check` immediately after `full-suite-gate` guarantees GREEN already passed. Because `STRICT_VERDICT_PHASE_NAMES` at `src/execution/story-orchestrator/types.ts:222` only contains strict pass/fail phases, the new phase must stay out of that set so survivors remain warnings only and downstream phases still execute.

Builder and plan wiring already follow highly regular patterns. `StoryOrchestratorBuilder` in `src/execution/story-orchestrator/builder.ts:33-115` has overload pairs such as `addFullSuiteGate(...)` and `addVerifyScoped(...)` that call `setPhase(...)` with either a provided slot or the default exported op. The new `addMutationCheck(...)` should mirror that pattern rather than introducing a special-case builder API. `PlanInputs` in `src/execution/plan-inputs.ts:35` is the typed envelope for all optional slots, so it needs a `mutationCheck?: MutationCheckInput` field adjacent to the existing verification-related slots. `buildPlanForStrategy()` in `src/execution/build-plan-for-strategy.ts:83` is the SSOT for strategy-dependent plan construction, so it is the only correct place to conditionally add the mutation-check phase when the input is present.

The operation barrel is a required integration point. `src/operations/index.ts` currently exports `greenfieldGateOp`, `fullSuiteGateOp`, and `verifyScopedOp`, and `StoryOrchestratorBuilder` imports concrete operations from that barrel. If `mutationCheckOp` and its types are not exported there, the plan-wiring story cannot satisfy the spec AC that imports the op from `@/operations`.

The existing tests strongly support this feature shape. Config defaults and merge behavior are already covered by unit suites such as `test/unit/config/flake-detection-schema.test.ts`, `test/unit/config/merge.test.ts`, and `test/unit/config/selectors.test.ts`, which makes them the right pattern references for US-001. Deterministic operation behavior and DI-style operation tests are already established by `test/unit/operations/greenfield-gate.test.ts` and `test/unit/operations/verify-scoped.test.ts`. Story-orchestrator and builder/plan seams already have extensive coverage in `test/unit/execution/story-orchestrator.test.ts`, `test/unit/execution/plan-inputs.test.ts`, `test/unit/execution/builder-extensibility.test.ts`, and the `test/integration/tdd/story-orchestrator-*.test.ts` suites. The mutation feature should extend those areas rather than inventing a separate harness.

Backward compatibility is simple but important. The feature is opt-in with `execution.mutationCheck.enabled` defaulting to `false`, so existing runs must behave exactly as they do today unless the setting is enabled. The critical compatibility protections are: disabled config must short-circuit without selecting scoped tests or running regression, unsupported languages must no-op rather than error, survivor results must not be treated as gate failures, and plans without a `mutationCheck` input must build without adding a new phase. There is no data migration or persisted-state migration; the implementation order should stay as the spec already lays out: config subtree first, pure mutation core second, apply/classify layer third, operation fourth, and phase wiring last.
